resale_co.name: Certificate of Inspection for Transfer of Title (Certificate of Occupancy on sale)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Spring Lake Heights Zoning / Code Enforcement Officer (Public Officer)
resale_co.lead_time: The Borough code adds a surcharge when the application is filed less than 10 calendar days before occupancy.
requirements: Inspection of the home before transfer of title or occupancy
Signed owner certification that smoke and CO alarms are installed and working, plus the smoke/CO inspection (see fire certificate)

Exterior: roof, gutters, siding, fences, windows, screens and doors in good condition; handrails on stairs with three or more risers; guardrail gaps no more than 5 inches; house number at least 3 inches visible from the street; no debris
Driveway must have an apron and a paved, brick, paver or stone surface; sidewalk, curb, driveway and apron free of cracks, trip hazards or standing water
No open construction permits; all work done during ownership must have been permitted and passed final inspection
Municipal taxes, water and sewer should be paid up to date

Interior: no bedrooms in basements or more than 2 feet below grade; bedroom size minimums; GFI outlets within 6 feet of water; stove anti-tip bracket and gas shut off valves; emergency furnace switch; keyless interior deadbolts; no sump pump discharge into the sewer
Wood burning fireplaces and stoves certified by a certified chimney sweep company
Secondary power source warning label within 18 inches of the electric panel and meter for homes with a generator, solar or battery storage (P.L.2025, c.19)
Zoning permit also required for transfer of title of anything other than a single family home
Application lists sale price, closing and occupancy dates, buyer and all occupants with dates of birth

fees.label: Certificate of Inspection, transfer of title for a single family dwelling
fees.quote: Transfer of Title for Single Family Dwelling $200.00 per dwelling

fees.label: Certificate of Inspection, transfer of title for a two-family, multi-family or apartment building
fees.quote: Transfer of Title for Two-family, Multi-Family or Apartment Building $15 per unit + $200.00 /bldg.

fees.label: Zoning permit for transfer of title (all uses except single family)
fees.quote: Zoning Permit also required for Transfer of Title for all uses except Single Family $100.00

fees.label: Reinspection, per dwelling unit or building
fees.quote: Re-Inspection if necessary $50.00 per dwelling unit or bldg

fees.label: Late filing surcharge, 6 to 9 calendar days before occupancy (Borough code)
fees.quote: Additional fee required from applicants seeking a Certificate of Occupancy with no more than 6 days but less than 10 calendar days prior to occupancy$50 additional

fees.label: Late filing surcharge, 5 calendar days or less before occupancy (Borough code)
fees.quote: Additional fee required from applicants seeking a Certificate of Occupancy with 5 calendar days or less prior to occupancy$100 additional

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Borough's 2026 Certificate of Inspection Application (Rental and Transfer of Title), including the signed smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm certification, and file it with the fee at the Municipal Building, 555 Brighton Avenue (Zoning/Code Enforcement office hours Monday and Wednesday, 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM). Fees are non-refundable and non-transferable.

resale_co.notes: Building and Housing Section 10-2.7 (read in full through the ecode360 print view; last amendment listed Ord. No. 2018-09) requires a Certificate of Occupancy before any sale or transfer of title and lists older fees: Title transfers (sales) $100, sales of multi-family dwellings $15 per unit and $100 per building, reinspection $25, plus late filing surcharges of $50 (6 to 9 days) and $100 (5 days or less). The Borough's 2026 application shows higher fees ($200.00 single family, $15 per unit + $200.00 per building for two-family and larger, $50.00 reinspection); the newer form is listed as the main fee, and the code surcharges are listed because the form does not mention them. Confirm which apply. Rental-only items (landlord registration, liability insurance, lead-safe certificate with a $20 state fee, short-term rental license) are not resale requirements.

requirements: Smoke alarms tested by push button; homes built before 1978 need at least battery alarms on each level and near bedrooms; 1978 to 1983 hardwired with battery backup; 1984 to 1990 also interconnected; 1991 and later also one in each bedroom
Battery-only smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed units; detectors over 10 years old are not accepted
Monitored systems need a letter from the owner, agent or monitoring company
Carbon monoxide alarms outside each separate sleeping area where there are fuel burning appliances or an attached garage; not older than 5 years or past the maker's expiration date
Fire extinguisher of the correct size, properly mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen (form still lists it)
Owner signs a certification that the smoke and CO alarms are installed and working

authorities.name: Spring Lake Heights Bureau of Fire Prevention (with the Zoning Office, as part of the Certificate of Inspection)
authorities.how_to_apply: The smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm certification is a page of the Borough's Certificate of Inspection application and is checked at that inspection; no separate smoke/CO fee is published. Questions go to the Fire Official, Chris Willms (firemarshal@springlakehts.com).

fire_cert.notes: The state fire directory lists the Spring Lake Heights Zoning Office as the smoke detector compliance office, with Christopher Willms as fire official. The Fire Prevention page phone (732-449-9433 ex. 118) is the same number Sea Girt lists for him, while the Borough's main number is 732-449-3500. The 2026 form still lists a fire extinguisher even though P.L.2025, c.19 dropped it from the state sale certificate in February 2025; the same form adds the new secondary power source label from that law.

other_items.label: Sidewalk, curb, driveway and apron
other_items.detail: Must be in good condition, free of cracks, trip hazards or standing water; driveways need an apron and a finished surface. Checked at the Certificate of Inspection.

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: All open construction permits must have a passed final inspection on file before the inspection.

other_items.label: Taxes, water and sewer
other_items.detail: Municipal taxes, water and sewer should be paid up to date.

other_items.label: Chimney certification
other_items.detail: Wood burning fireplaces and stoves must be certified safe by a certified chimney sweep company.

other_items.label: Zoning permit for non single family sales
other_items.detail: A $100.00 zoning permit is also required for transfer of title of anything other than a single family home (so a two-family sale needs one).

open_questions: Do the code's late filing surcharges ($50 under 10 days, $100 at 5 days or less) still apply with the 2026 fee schedule?
